subject: Mathematics
summary: A comprehensive axiomatic exploration of set theory from Russell's paradox and ZFC foundations to interval topologies on the real line ℝ, power set combinatorics, Boolean set algebra, rigorous mutual inclusion proofs for De Morgan's laws, the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion (PIE) with Bonferroni bounds, characteristic indicator functions, high-yield examination traps, and 20 NEST-calibrated practice problems.
chapterCommonMistakes: Misconception 1: Thinking ∅, {∅}, and {{}} are identical sets. Reality: ∅ is empty (|∅| = 0), while {∅} is a singleton set (|{∅}| = 1). Thus ∅ ∈ {∅} is TRUE, but ∅ = {∅} is FALSE.

Misconception 2: Assuming the power set distributes over union: 𝒫(A ∪ B) = 𝒫(A) ∪ 𝒫(B). Reality: False! In general, 𝒫(A) ∪ 𝒫(B) ⊊ 𝒫(A ∪ B) because 𝒫(A ∪ B) contains subsets formed by mixing elements from both A and B.
Misconception 3: Believing the open interval (a, a) contains the single point a. Reality: The open interval (a, a) = {x ∈ ℝ | a < x < a} = ∅. Only the closed interval [a, a] = {a} is a singleton set.

Misconception 4: Applying cancellation law to set intersections: A ∩ B = A ∩ C ⟹ B = C. Reality: False! B and C can differ arbitrarily outside set A. B = C requires BOTH A ∩ B = A ∩ C and A ∪ B = A ∪ C.
Misconception 5: Assuming the symmetric difference A △ B is non-associative. Reality: False! (A △ B) △ C = A △ (B △ C). (𝒫(U), △) forms an Abelian Group with identity ∅.

Misconception 6: Conflating countable infinity with uncountably infinite cardinality. Reality: |ℕ| = |ℤ| = |ℚ| = ℵ₀ (Countably infinite), whereas |(0, 1)| = |ℝ| = c = 2^ℵ₀ > ℵ₀ (Uncountably infinite).

Misconception 7: Thinking subset relation A ⊆ B implies A has strictly fewer elements than B. Reality: A ⊆ B permits A = B. In infinite sets, proper subsets can have identical cardinality (|2ℕ| = |ℕ| = ℵ₀).

keyTerms.definition: An unordered collection of unique objects defined by an explicit membership criterion.
A self-contradictory statement within an axiomatic system (e.g., Russell's Paradox).
A one-to-one and onto mapping between two sets establishing cardinal equivalence.
The total number of elements in a set A. Equals n for finite sets; ℵ₀ for countable; c for continuum.
The set of all ordered pairs (a, b) such that a ∈ A and b ∈ B. |A × B| = |A| · |B|.
An indicator function mapping elements to 1 if x ∈ A and 0 if x ∉ A.
The set of all elements in the universal set U that do not belong to A.
Fundamental set identities: (A ∪ B)' = A' ∩ B' and (A ∩ B)' = A' ∪ B'.
Sets A and B whose intersection is empty (A ∩ B = ∅).
The mathematical driver behind the Principle of Inclusion-Exclusion (PIE).
The unique set containing zero elements (|∅| = 0). Vacuously a subset of every set A.
A set whose elements can be placed in bijection with {1, 2, ..., n} for some n ∈ ℕ₀.
A connected subset of real numbers defined by upper and lower boundary points.
A collection of non-empty mutually disjoint subsets of A whose union equals A.
The set of all subsets of A, having cardinality 2^{|A|}.
A subset A of B such that A ≠ B.
The set of elements in A that are not in B.
The set of elements in A ∪ B but not in A ∩ B.
The master set containing all objects under consideration in a particular context.
A visual representation of set operations using overlapping closed planar regions.
